title: आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा शिक्षाको निरन्तरता
nepali: ‘विपद्’ कुनै पनि समय, स्थान र परिस्थितिमा देखा पर्न सक्छ । संसारका सबैजसो देश र समुदायले कुनै न कुनै विपद्को सामना गरिरहेको देख्न, सुन्न पाइन्छ । प्राकृतिक कारणले होस् वा मानवीय कारणले होस्, विपद्ले सामान्यतया सम्बन्धित देशका सबै नागरिकहरूलाई असर गर्ने भए पनि खासगरी बुढाबुढी, बालबालिका, अपाङ्गता भएकाहरू, महिला तथा रोगीहरूलाई अझ बढी नकारात्मक प्रभाव पारेको भेटिन्छ । धन सम्पत्ति, सार्वजनिक भवन र संरचनाहरू मात्र नभएर विपद्ले व्यक्तिको ज्यान समेत लिने भएकोले यसले तत्कालिन र दीर्घकालिन सबैखाले दुष्प्रभावको सामना गर्न मानिसहरूलाई बाध्य गराउँछ । यसले धन सम्पत्तिको विनास, पारिवारिक विघटन, कसैको उठीबास लगाउने मात्र नभै बसाईं सर्न बाध्य गराउने, चोट ग्रस्त पार्ने तथा कतिपय अवस्थामा नागरिकहरूको सामान्य अधिकारबाट समेत विमुख बनाई दिन सक्छ । सामान्य गाँसबास, औषधीमूलो, आवतजावत गर्न पाउने स्वतन्त्रता मात्र होइन, बालबालिकाको पढ्न र सिक्न पाउने अधिकारबाट एकै झ्टकामा अधिकार बिहिन बनाई दिएको देख्न पाइन्छ । व्यक्तिको बाँच्न पाउने, सुरक्षित हुन पाउने तथा अन्य नागरिक हक र सेवाहरूलाई विपद्ले निष्प्रभावी बनाई दिने हुँदा यसबाट सामाजिक, आर्थिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा पारिवरिक अवस्थामा पर्ने प्रभाव÷दुष्प्रभावहरूलाई अझबढी नियाल्नु पर्ने हुन जान्छ । विपद्को एउटै घटनाले शिक्षामा पार्ने असरबाट समाजका लाखौं विद्यार्थीहरू सिक्न पाउने नैसर्गिक हकबाट बञ्चित हुन परेको घटना २०७२ सालको भूकम्पले दर्शाइ सकेको छ । पठनपाठनको अवसरबाट लाखौं विद्यार्थीहरू लामो समयसम्म विमुख हुन नपसोस् भन्ने अभिप्रायले राज्यद्वारा जे–जति शैक्षिक प्रयत्नहरू गरिए, तिनै कोसिसहरूको सन्दर्भमा यो सामग्री तयार गरिएको छ ।
american_english: 'Disaster' can appear at any time, place, and circumstance. It can be seen and heard that almost all countries and communities in the world are facing one or another disaster. Whether due to natural causes or human causes, although disaster generally affects all citizens of the concerned country, it is found to have a more negative impact especially on the elderly, children, persons with disabilities, women, and the sick. Not only wealth and property, public buildings, and structures, but because disaster can even take a person's life, it compels people to face all kinds of immediate and long-term adverse effects. It can destroy wealth and property, break up families, and uproot someone, and not only that but also force relocation, cause injury, and in some cases even deprive citizens of their ordinary rights. It can be seen that not only the freedom to have basic food and shelter, medicine, and movement, but also the right of children to read and learn is taken away in a single stroke. Because disaster renders ineffective a person's right to live, right to be safe, and other citizen rights and services, the impacts and adverse impacts falling on social, economic, cultural, and family conditions must be observed all the more. The event of millions of students of society being deprived of their natural right to learn from the effect that a single disaster event has on education has already been shown by the earthquake of 2072 BS. With the intention that millions of students should not be deprived of the opportunity of teaching and learning for a long time, this material has been prepared in the context of whatever educational efforts were made by the state.

informal_english: A disaster can pop up any time, anywhere, in any situation. You see and hear about nearly every country and community around the world copping one disaster or another. Whether it's natural or human-caused, disasters generally hit everyone in the affected country, but they hit the elderly, kids, people with disabilities, women and the sick especially hard. It's not just money and property, public buildings and structures - disasters can even take lives, so people are forced to deal with all sorts of immediate and long-term fallout. They can wipe out wealth and property, tear families apart, uproot people, force them to relocate, injure them, and in some cases even strip citizens of their ordinary rights. You can see that not only basic needs like food, shelter, medicine and getting around, but even kids' right to read and learn gets taken away in one hit. Because disasters knock out a person's right to live, right to be safe and other citizen rights and services, we need to keep a closer eye on how they affect social, economic, cultural and family life. The 2072 BS earthquake already showed how a single disaster event can rob millions of students of their natural right to learn. This material has been put together with the aim that millions of students don't get shut out of teaching and learning for ages, drawing on whatever educational efforts the state made.
